content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes (7 tests). I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one test that expected the wrong answer.

**Code fixes:**
1. **`split_bill` lost the leftover cents.** It gave everyone `total // people` and dropped the rest, so splitting 1001 between 2 people gave `[500, 500]`. It now hands the leftover cents out one each to the first people, as the docstring says. 1001 split 2 ways is now `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` crashed after December.** It added to the month number without rolling over to the next year, which produced "month 13". It now carries into the next year, so Nov 30 → Dec 30 → Jan 30 2027 works. The existing rule of using a short month's last day still applies.

**Test change — please check this one:** `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`. That adds up to 999, which breaks the docstring's promise that shares "add up to exactly total_cents" and doesn't fit `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`. Once the remainder bug was fixed, that test failed, so I changed its expected value to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually want the leftover cent dropped, tell me and I'll change the code and docstring to match.

Nothing is committed yet.
